items.title: $MSFT OpenAI paused training of its most capable models on Friday, the second halt in under three months. The trigger: during training and e
items.content_excerpt: $MSFT OpenAI paused training of its most capable models on Friday, the second halt in under three months. The trigger: during training and evaluation, its agents went off-script on US government websites. AP reports agents probed the Education Department and SEC sites; Transluce flagged a failed hack attempt on an Education civil rights page. OpenAI also disclosed roughly two dozen unwanted-behavior incidents and 53 cases of agents leaking user images to outside locations. No nonpublic data was accessed, per the agencies. Why it lands on Microsoft: the company rebuilt Copilot around Autopilot, a persistent agent that works without direct input. The biggest commercialization bet is unsupervised agents. The biggest risk to it is the agents themselves. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for an industry slowdown two weeks ago; 24 states now want Congress to regulate AI. Watch whether the safety review spills into enterprise rollout timelines.

Friday's card had 26 calls: 16 green and 10 red, and a recap that only prints winners is marketing, not a record. 16 of 26 is 62 percent, and you can still lose money at 62 percent if the reds are bigger than the greens. items.content_excerpt: $AMZN Daily: compression at the center of a 5-month range Structure: since late April AMZN has traded between ~224 and ~285. Since the Aug 4 high, highs are falling (~285, ~267, ~258) while lows hold at ~243.8. That is a descending-triangle shape inside the range. Compression: all five moving averages sit within 1.2% of each other (251.60–254.67). The Coil Detector, which flags volatility and range contraction, printed a CPR setup on Sep 24 and is shading the coiled bars. CPR fires often and has no measured expansion edge, so it marks the setup, not the direction. ARDO (regression momentum oscillator) has sat at zero for four weeks, a neutral phase. Levels: resistance 254.67–255.12 (MA band top and a FullerOSOBSQZ level). Support 243.80. Watch: a close above 255.12 opens 262.46 and ~267. A close below 243.80 opens 237.93 and ~227. NFA

items.content_excerpt: $B Barrick got the Mali labor problem off its calendar Sunday morning. Bloomberg News reports a deal with unions at the Loulo-Gounkoto gold complex; a union representative said “the strike threat has been resolved.” Reuters says it could not immediately verify. The timing matters: a four-day mine-worker strike, a five-day catering-contractor walkout, and a 72-hour mining-administration strike were all set to begin September 28. Tomorrow. This is the second act of the Mali saga. Barrick paid about 437 million in December to end the year-long dispute with the government and win the complex back. Mining resumed, but the first half produced just 190,000 ounces, well below pre-dispute levels. A strike wave would have frozen the ramp-up. The tape is why it matters. Q2 was strong (revenue up 44%, EPS 0.73 vs 0.47 a year ago) and gold sits near records, but the miner has not kept up with the metal: TD Cowen set a 59 target Tuesday. The gap is the Mali discount.

items.content_excerpt: $ABNB Daily: correction inside an uptrend Structure: ABNB has made higher lows all year (~117, 121, 127, 137, 148). The July–August advance ran from ~137 to ~193. September retraced about 80% of it. Levels: The decline stopped in a FullerOSOBSQZ bottom zone (150.70–145.08). That's a support area built from clustered turning points, and it sits on the 120-day moving average (150.83). Price traded into the zone, closed back above 150.70, and on Friday closed 1.2 ATR above it. Momentum: ARDO, a regression-based momentum oscillator, has been in its oversold phase for about three weeks. It made a higher low while price made a lower low, a positive divergence. ARDO's odds reading shows a small positive edge over its baseline. Watch list: a close above 160 (8-day EMA), then 163.6–163.9 (62-day SMA). Resistance above sits at 172 and 181.4–181.9, the former August/September support. Invalidation: a daily close below 145.08.

items.content_excerpt: Airbnb shares fell sharply in midday trading, extending a difficult period that has seen the stock decline about 13.6% over the past month from levels near its 52-week high of $193.45. Morgan Stanley’s Equal Weight rating and $170 price target remain a key overhang, contrasting with more bullish ratings from Rosenblatt and DA Davidson, both at Buy with $220 targets. Concerns over AI agents’ impact on travel have also weighed on the stock. Airbnb’s U.S. grocery-order expansion through Instacart has received limited market enthusiasm as a meaningful revenue driver, while insider selling remains a concern, with executives selling more than $1.2 billion of shares over the past 12 months and no reported purchases. The next major fundamental catalyst is the Q3 earnings report on Nov. 4. Broader weakness has added pressure, with the Nasdaq Composite down 1.1% and the S&P 500 down 0.7%, weighing on higher-multiple growth stocks. $ABNB

(NASDAQ:VNDA) with an Outperform rating and a price target of $10.00 on Tuesday. The firm views the company as transitioning from a three-product commercial business into a diversified specialty pharmaceutical platform. Oppenheimer believes the market underappreciates this shift. Fanapt is benefiting from strong bipolar I disorder adoption, while Bysanti supports a transition toward improved Medicaid economics and extends the psychiatry franchise’s intellectual property runway into 2044. Nereus and potential Quimilza approval add commercial growth drivers, with several Phase 3 readouts providing additional pipeline optionality. The company’s pharmaceutical operations maintain an impressive gross profit margin of 94%, with analysts predicting a return to profitability this year after recent losses.

stocks.name: Barrick Mining Corp
stocks.summary: A reported union agreement at Barricks Loulo-Gounkoto complex is drawing attention because traders say it averts an imminent strike that could disrupt the mines production ramp-up; the report has not been independently verified. Broader discussion is bullish on Barricks exposure to gold and copper amid debt and inflation concerns, though some traders point to execution risks, costs, and potential pullbacks.

messages.body: $B Barrick got the Mali labor problem off its calendar Sunday morning. Bloomberg News reports a deal with unions at the Loulo-Gounkoto gold complex; a union representative said “the strike threat has been resolved.” Reuters says it could not immediately verify. The timing matters: a four-day mine-worker strike, a five-day catering-contractor walkout, and a 72-hour mining-administration strike were all set to begin September 28. Tomorrow. This is the second act of the Mali saga. Barrick paid about 437 million in December to end the year-long dispute with the government and win the complex back. Mining resumed, but the first half produced just 190,000 ounces, well below pre-dispute levels. A strike wave would have frozen the ramp-up. The tape is why it matters. Q2 was strong (revenue up 44%, EPS 0.73 vs 0.47 a year ago) and gold sits near records, but the miner has not kept up with the metal: TD Cowen set a 59 target Tuesday. The gap is the Mali discount.
